newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Repsol share sale success assured.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Repsol share sale success assured.

text.p: The offer of the Spanish state's remaining 10 percent stake in energy group Repsol, which starts on Monday, is expected to be a success based on its growth potential and acceptance among investors, analysts say.
"Our recommendation for the share is a strong buy and we believe that it could have a proportional result similar to that of Telefonica," an analyst with Ahorro Corporacion Financiera said.

The majority of dealers consulted compared Repsol's placement to the hugely successful sale of the last state-owned piece of telecoms group Telefonica in February, in terms of both the volume of demand and the share price development.

"If Telefonica shares rise in the next few days, it will benefit the Repsol sale because many of the applications will be from the same investors," said one analyst from a bank underwriting the placement.
Telefonica shares were offered to retail investors at 3,239 pesetas and to institutions at 3,360 pesetas. They were trading at 3,300 at the close on Friday.
Another factor seen weighing in Repsol's favour was the small size of the offer compared with that of Telefonica, 23 million and 171 million shares respectively.
"It's a relatively simple placement because it's small," a broker with ABN-Amro said. "After the previous experiences, the retail tranche will be placed without any type of problem."

Most analysts believe there will be oversubscription for the retail offer because of very heavy demand from individual Spanish investors, just as there was for Telefonica and for fashion house Adolfo Dominguez, which went public last month.
The institutional tranches were also seen selling without a hitch, though without such strong demand because of the near-term placements of other European firms in the sector.
The state's holding in Repsol, mainly involved in the exploration, production, refining and marketing of crude oil, is around 30 million shares.

"Repsol is one of the most liquid shares on the bourse and if I want to increase the weight of my portfolios I can do so even if it's trading at a price that is not very different from the share offer price," the head of a mutual funds unit said.

Spain's state holding company SEPI said it was initially offering 4.5 million shares to employees, 12.75 million to retail investors and 10.2 million to institutions. Retail investors will be offered a four percent discount.
Analysts said the share offer price could end up higher than the current level but it would still be a good deal. Repsol closed at 5,840 pesetas on Friday.
In trading this year, the stock price has hit a high of 6,100 pesetas on March 17 and a low of 4,905 on January 2.
"To buy Repsol at the current price is very safe and we could see a share offer price at around 6,300, with a four percent discount for the retail tranche," the Ahorro Corporacion analyst said.
"The current prices, and even something a little higher for the share offer, don't surprise anyone."
